All biologically feasible equilibria are characterized, and local and global asymptotic stability conditions are derived using Matignon’s criterion and Lyapunov function techniques. The analysis further reveals that the coexistence equilibrium can lose stability through a Hopf bifurcation induced by the fractional memory order, and a critical threshold for the onset of this bifurcation is derived. Numerical evaluation of the first Lyapunov coefficient provides evidence that the bifurcation is supercritical, leading to the emergence of stable periodic oscillations. Applying Pontryagin’s Maximum Principle, we derive a bang–singular–bang optimal harvesting strategy that improves discounted net revenue while maintaining ecologically sustainable population levels. Numerical simulations support the theoretical results and illustrate the combined influence of fear, refuge, anti-predator behavior, harvesting, and memory on ecosystem dynamics. The findings demonstrate that the fractional memory order acts as an effective regulator of ecological stability, providing a biologically interpretable mechanism for controlling oscillatory behavior that has no counterpart in classical integer-order predator–prey models.
nce431fda5920: Background India has committed to achieving ‘Eliminate Tuberculosis (TB)’ by 2025. The Government of India issued guidelines regarding the crucial strategy of Tuberculosis Preventive Treatment in July 2021. Objectives To identify factors influencing tuberculosis preventive treatment program implementation and acceptance of tuberculosis preventive treatment. Methods We conducted the study in the Pune district from April to August 2024. It was a qualitative study using Focus Group Discussions (FGD) with Medical Officers (MO) and adult contacts of the index case, and In-depth Interviews (IDI) with senior health officers. We conducted eight FGDs with MOs and six with adult contacts, and conducted in-depth interviews with senior health officers. Data were transcribed, translated, and analyzed using MAXQDA. Results Eighty-six health/medical officers and 43 adult contacts participated in FGD and IDI. Some health officers have received training in tuberculosis but not in preventive treatment. Knowledge about tuberculosis preventive treatment and duration was minimal. Medical officers minimally briefed contacts. Stigma mainly from contacts perspectives, migration from health personnels perspectives and lack of awareness from both the groups emerged as important factors influencing screening and treatment of adult contacts. Very few underwent blood/ X-ray/ sputum testing, and fewer received treatment for varied durations. Medical officers knew only the isoniazid regimen, and interferon-gamma release assay testing was either unknown or unavailable. There is a shortage of trained human resources. The supply of diagnostic kits and medicines was disrupted. Health personnel and contacts recommended non-pharmacological measures such as mask use, cleanliness, and good nutrition. All officers perceived that elimination may linger until 2030. Training, counselling, community awareness, and multi-sectoral collaboration were strategies suggested by health officers. Conclusions Health personnel capacity building, strengthening infrastructure and logistics, multiple strategies to mitigate stigma, and multi-sectoral collaboration are needed to satisfactory implementation of TB preventive treatment.
n4bb4217e54c3: Background Chronic musculoskeletal pain is highly prevalent among older adults and is associated with disability, reduced physical activity, and decreased quality of life. Digital health interventions can improve access to care and support pain self-management. InControl is a user-centered web-based platform that combines exercise and pain science education. The aim of this pilot study is to assess the usability and acceptability of the InControl platform and the feasibility of the research methods. This will help inform methodological improvements in the design of a future randomized controlled trial. Methods A randomized, parallel-group, mixed-methods pilot study will be conducted with two groups: usual care group and the InControl intervention. Thirty-four participants aged 60 years or older with chronic musculoskeletal pain will be recruited at the Local Health Unit of Aveiro Region. The InControl intervention will last 8 weeks and will combine in-person sessions with remote interventions. Feasibility will be assessed using indicators of recruitment, retention, adherence, refusal, and dropout rates. Usability will be measured using the System Usability Scale, while acceptability and appropriateness will be assessed through a questionnaire and semi-structured interviews. Secondary outcomes will include pain, physical function, psychological factors, quality of life, and cognitive function. Data will be analyzed using descriptive statistics and qualitative thematic analysis. Discussion The findings will inform the design of a future large-scale randomized controlled trial and contribute to the development of more effective digital interventions tailored to the needs of older adults with chronic musculoskeletal pain. Trial registration This study is registered on clinicaltrials.gov, NCT07774416 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07774416?tab=study), August 18, 2026.
n4b4a47f7176e: We extend the delayed reaction–diffusion SI model with nonlinear incidence proposed by Song et al. by replacing the fixed transmission lag with weak and strong gamma-distributed memory kernels. Because the model has no exposed compartment, the memory term is interpreted phenomenologically as a distributed timing of transmission-related effects of past infectious states rather than as an explicit latent-stage mechanism. Using the same parameter set adopted by Song et al., we show that the distributed-memory models have a stability structure that is qualitatively different from that of the discrete-delay model. For the spatially homogeneous mode, both gamma kernels exhibit a small stabilising spectral Hopf crossing at a mean memory time near 0.08. The discrete-delay model has a comparable small stabilising crossing but, in addition, a much larger destabilising crossing near τ=1.335. Consequently, at the nominal values 1.2 and 1.6 used in the reference simulations, the gamma models converge to the selected endemic equilibrium, whereas the discrete-delay model crosses into an oscillatory regime. The first spatial mode is different: for the gamma formulations its modal constant term is negative for every positive memory rate, so this mode is unstable for every positive mean-memory value. We therefore interpret this behavior as a memory-independent spatial-mode instability, distinct from both a memory-induced Hopf crossing and a classical Turing instability.
n6313663b8375: Groundwater chemistry reflects both natural and anthropogenic processes. In rapidly urbanizing areas where agricultural and construction land coexist, differences in shallow groundwater chemistry remain poorly understood. This study compared hydrochemical characteristics between agricultural and construction land-use types in the Jining National High-tech Zone, China, using geochemical diagrams, ion ratios, mineral saturation indices, and multivariate statistics. Groundwater in the study area was generally neutral to weakly alkaline, with pH 6.78–7.51 in agricultural samples and 7.19–7.47 in construction samples. Agricultural groundwater had higher mean TDS (797.28 vs 624.00 mg/L in construction groundwater) but lower variation, suggesting spatially uniform carbonate dissolution. Conversely, construction groundwater displayed higher mean Na+ concentrations (59.85 mg/L) and greater hydrochemical heterogeneity. After Holm correction, pH, TDS, total hardness, and Ca2+ differed significantly between the two land-use types (adjusted p 3-N, did not. The Cl- coefficient of variation exceeded 100% in construction areas, and NO3-N variability was elevated in agricultural areas. These patterns indicate mixed influences from silicate weathering, cation exchange, and localized anthropogenic inputs. Principal component analysis yielded three components: PC1 (44.62%) represented a mineralization gradient, PC2 (17.08%) reflected pH–alkalinity balance, and PC3 (14.17%) indicated silicate weathering versus carbonate dissolution. PC1 and PC2 scores differed significantly among land-use types (p = 0.007 and 0.009, respectively), but PC3 scores did not (p = 0.826). Overall, agricultural groundwater showed carbonate-dissolution dominance with pronounced nitrate enrichment (NO3-N 102.7%), while construction groundwater showed silicate-influenced, Na-Cl-coupled signatures with greater heterogeneity (Cl- 106.6%). These results link land-use differences to distinct shallow groundwater hydrochemical patterns, though such patterns may reflect combined influences of land use, hydrogeological setting, and aquifer lithology. The findings underscore the need for land-use-specific groundwater management in rapidly urbanizing agricultural-industrial regions and provide a baseline for future process-oriented research.
n5e2d6439f4eb: Dynamic changes in physiological oxygen levels are crucial for proper cortical brain development. In this context, oxygen is important not only for its role in energy metabolism but also as a signaling molecule. While much is already known about its most prominent signaling factor hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-1α, little is known about its functionally similar isoform HIF-2α during cortical development. Therefore, we utilized HIF-2α conditional knock-out mice (Emx1 and Nestin driven), which were kept under maternal hypoxia (10% pO2), physioxia (21% pO2), or hyperoxia (75% pO2) starting at E14.5 for 48 h and analyzed their cortical development by immunohistochemistry at E16.5. The analysis of newborn neurons (BrdU+) and cortical layer IV (Tbr1+), V (Ctip2+), and upper layer neurons (Satb2+) revealed clear effects of oxygen, with hyperoxia particularly increasing the number of Ctip2+/Tbr1- layer V neurons in E16.5 fetuses. However, neither the number of newborn neurons nor the number of layer-specific neurons was affected by HIF-2α CKO. Similarly, oxygen-related effects on neural stem cells (NSCs) and neuroprogenitor cells were not mediated by HIF-2α in E16.5 fetuses. Contributing, in vitro expansion and stem cell maintenance of NSCs were accelerated by physioxia (3% pO2) compared to hyperoxia (21% pO2), without involvement of HIF-2α under either condition. In conclusion, oxygen modulates cortical development, but HIF-2α does not mediate these effects. Thus, oxygen-related changes in neurogenesis and cortical morphology appear to be regulated via HIF-2α-independent mechanisms.
n73bb7590ec45: Background Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is widely reported as cost-effective, but reported incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) are shaped by model structure, assumptions, comparator choice, vaccine price, threshold selection, and local screening context. Previous reviews have summarized cost-effectiveness findings but have less often examined why conclusions differ across settings. Objective To map methodological evolution, drivers of variation, reporting completeness, methodological credibility, and transferability in HPV vaccination economic evaluations. Methods A scoping review was conducted using the methodological framework proposed by Arksey and O’Malley, refined by Levac et al., and informed by JBI guidance for scoping reviews. Reporting followed PRISMA-ScR, and the protocol was preregistered on the Open Science Framework (OSF). PubMed, Scopus, PsycINFO, Embase, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025, with a final search conducted on January 2, 2026. Forty-four records were mapped. Thirty-three full comparative economic evaluations formed the primary synthesis; 11 partial or non-standard economic evidence records were retained as contextual evidence. The Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) checklist was applied retrospectively to assess reporting completeness, and a descriptive structured appraisal was used to examine methodological credibility across six health-economic domains. A Welte-informed assessment was used to examine target-context contextualization. Results The evidence base evolved from early static cohort models to dynamic transmission and individual-based approaches, while static models remained common in LMIC-focused standardized-tool analyses. The main drivers of variation were vaccine price, discounting, herd-immunity assumptions, cross-protection assumptions, and threshold selection. Reporting completeness varied and did not necessarily correspond to methodological credibility. Relevance to a study’s own decision setting did not imply that its ICER could be transferred to other countries. Eleven contextual records showed emerging policy questions around delivery costs, fiscal consequences, uptake, risk-benefit framing, and non-ICER-based decision support. Conclusion The economic value reported for HPV vaccination depends on the assumptions, comparators, vaccine prices, thresholds, and local screening contexts used in each evaluation rather than on the vaccine alone. Future evaluations should explicitly justify the choice of comparator, model structure, vaccine-price assumptions, discount rates, thresholds, uncertainty analysis, and transferability assumptions. Although formal cost-effectiveness analyses of single-dose HPV vaccination have begun to emerge, evidence remains limited, particularly regarding durability, waning, delivery feasibility, gender-neutral vaccination in LMICs, and country-specific evaluations in underrepresented regions.
n6c7ee5ac52d4: Colombia has become the principal host of Venezuelan migrants in Latin America, prompting a complex mix of solidarity, anxiety, and discrimination. This study offers a multidimensional analysis of Twitter (now X) discourse on Venezuelan migration in Colombia between 2014 and 2022, using natural language processing, geolocation inference, sentiment analysis, and manual annotation of derogatory terms. Drawing from 7.4 million posts, we examine how online discourse evolves across time, space, and language. While negative sentiment is pronounced in original tweets during periods of political and social unrest, our findings highlight that users tend to amplify neutral and positive messages—over 67% of retweets fall into these categories—suggesting an informal counterbalance to polarized discourse. Additionally, the analysis of the derogatory terms veneco and veneca reveals significant gendered patterns: the feminine form veneca appears more frequently in negative contexts, pointing to the gendered dimensions of xenophobic language. These results underscore the dual function of social media as a site of both stigmatization and resistance, offering insights into the emotional and cultural dimensions of migration discourse in Colombia’s digital public sphere.
n17455c3a0f8e: African American (AA) men experience disproportionately high prostate cancer incidence and mortality. Despite this disparity, current genomic repositories are predominantly derived from European populations, and studies using archived tissues are often limited by stromal contamination. We sought to characterize the high-resolution somatic mutational landscape of AA prostate cancer using a high-fidelity, patient-matched model system to identify population-specific drivers and therapeutic targets. We performed whole-genome sequencing (WGS) on 10 matched pairs of primary cell cultures derived from prostate tumors and adjacent non-malignant tissues of AA patients. Our analyses revealed a complex, heterogeneous landscape characterized by significant genomic instability, including frequent chromothripsis and kataegis signatures. Mutation hotspots were concentrated on chromosomes 1, 2, 3, and X, with the highest mutation density on chromosome 17. Functionally impactful mutations were identified in critical oncogenic pathways, including chromatin remodeling (CHD1, ARID1A, ATRX, KDM6A) and DNA damage response (ATM, BRCA1/2, RAD51). Additionally, we identified potentially novel candidate mutations unique to this AA cohort, distinct from those in European-centric datasets. This study provides a foundational, patient-specific WGS dataset derived from African American prostate cancer cell models. The identification of high-frequency actionable alterations in epigenetic and DNA repair pathways highlights the utility of this renewable resource for developing tailored therapeutic interventions and addressing racial disparities in prostate cancer outcomes.
n515007e7ae08: Background Persons with albinism (PWAs) in Africa represent a vulnerable population facing social discrimination, severe health issues such as skin cancers, and precarious socioeconomic conditions. The objective of this study was to estimate the prevalence of albinism and map the distribution of persons with albinism in Togo in 2024. Method This cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted from November 2023 to October 2024 across all 39 health districts in Togo, and it included a telephone survey in which community health workers (CHWs) identified PWAs in their districts. CHWs were subsequently trained to perform onsite data collection using the Kobocollect application. Finally, the data were reviewed by national association representatives of PWAs to validate the data and address any gaps. The data were analysed using R software, while geographic mapping was performed with QGIS. Results A total of 1,521 PWAs were identified in Togo, which is a prevalence of 18.7 PWAs per 100,000 inhabitants (equivalent to 1/5,323; 95% CI [1/5,605; 1/5,065]). Sociodemographic and regional characteristics were available for 1,433 PWAs who consented to participate in this study and were included in the PWA database in Togo. Districts such as Kpélé, Danyi, and Amou presented the highest density of PWAs. The PWA population is predominantly young, with 62.7% under 25 years of age, and it has a slight female predominance (52.2%). Approximately 70.7% of PWAs reported daily exposure to the sun without adequate protection. Moreover, 61.6% had no regular income, and only 1.4% earned over 100 000 FCFA per month. Over 30% of PWAs experienced health issues related to albinism, yet only 37% had a medical follow-up record. Conclusion This first national study in Togo allowed us to estimate the prevalence of albinism in the country. The geographic distribution shows that PWAs are present throughout Togo, with concentrations in large cities. This type of research must continue to enable early identification and monitoring of PWAs to reduce the occurrence of serious health problems such as skin cancers.
n69150c0f830d: Objective To explore the effects and related mechanisms of a β-blocker combined with a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A receptor (5-HT1AR) agonist on MI injuries in rats. Methods TTC/Evans blue, H&E, Masson, and TUNEL staining were used to assess infarction area, pathological damage, fibrosis, and apoptosis in myocardial tissue. The ELISA kits were used to detect IL-1β and IL-18 levels. The immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was used in conjunction with qRT-PCR and Western blot to determine IL-1β, IL-18, NLRP3, pro Caspase-1, cleaved Caspase-1, GSDMD-FL, and GSDMD-N expression levels. Results In myocardial tissue, the β-blocker combined with the 5-HT1AR agonist effectively reduced infarction size, mitigated pathological injury, alleviated fibrosis, and prevented apoptosis. Meanwhile, the β-blocker combined with the 5-HT1AR agonist downregulated IL-1β and IL-18 levels in serum and myocardial tissue. Notably, although it barely altered the expression of the pyroptosis precursor proteins pro Caspase‑1 and GSDMD‑FL, the combined therapy strongly suppressed the mRNA and protein levels of NLRP3, cleaved Caspase‑1, and GSDMD‑N, and reduced the ratios of pro Caspase‑1/cleaved Caspase‑1 and GSDMD-FL/GSDMD-N in myocardial tissue. Conclusion β-blocker combined with the 5-HT1AR agonist relieves MI injuries by suppressing the NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD pathway.
na0325eb023b8: Theropod dinosaur remains from the Barremian (Lower Cretaceous) Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight, UK, are rare and often fragmentary. Here, we present a previously undescribed braincase from this formation that represents a new coelurosaurian, Invictibellatrix amberina gen. et sp. nov. Phylogenetic analysis and comparative anatomy indicate that Invictibellatrix is distantly related to all previously named theropods from this stratigraphic unit. Theropod braincases are often regarded as morphologically and phylogenetically conservative, but we demonstrate that neurocranial characters provide essential data that can help clarify the phylogenetic relationships of theropods. The sub-circular occipital condyle, sub-oval foramen magnum and presence of a sagittal nuchal crest indicate that Invictibellatrix is referable to Megaraptora, with phylogenetic analyses recovering it as an early-diverging member of this clade, within a paraphyletic array of Eurasian taxa. Incorporation of Invictibellatrix into a biogeographical analysis suggests that non-megaraptorid megaraptorans likely had a cosmopolitan distribution in the Early Cretaceous, and that the absence of megaraptorans in the Late Cretaceous of Laurasia is best explained by regional extinction. The recognition of this new genus increases our knowledge of Early Cretaceous European coelurosaurian diversity, which now includes tyrannosauroids, maniraptoriforms and megaraptorans.
n759fb0df395b: In past decades, conceptual analysis has established that evolution by natural selection (ENS) can occur without reproduction (Bouchard 2008 Philos. Sci. 75, 560–570 (doi:10.1086/594507); Papale, 2021 Synthese 198, 10 429–10 455 (doi:10.1007/s11229-020-02729-6)). The aim of this paper is to provide a computational proof of concept for this theoretical advance and to start assessing some of its conceptual upshots. To do so, we designed an agent-based model that introduces and defends a niche construction-based account of ENS without reproduction (ENSwR, pronounced like ‘answer’). Our results provide a computationally tractable proof of concept for ENSwR and a basis to reflect on some of its conceptual implications for debates regarding the origins of life. First, conceptual analysis suggests that ENSwR provides a novel explanatory framework that supports origins of life theories in which autocatalytic sets (ACSs) of chemical reactions play a central role (Xavier, Kauffman 2022 Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 380, 20210244 (doi:10.1098/rsta.2021.0244)). Second, through a discussion of the hydrothermal vent theory for the origins of life, we show that ENSwR will contribute to explaining the evolutionary origins of reproduction.
n9e969a1692e5: The herbicide 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) remains a relevant aquatic contaminant because parent-compound disappearance does not imply mineralization, detoxification or treatment readiness. This systematic review synthesizes recent evidence on advanced oxidation processes (AOPs) and closely related chemically coupled routes for aqueous 2,4-D treatment. Records from Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar within a documented 2020–2025 review window were screened using explicit eligibility criteria and assessed with an evidence-completeness rubric covering key reporting domains for cross-study comparison. The final corpus comprised 204 studies across photocatalytic/photo-assisted, electrochemical/electro-Fenton, Fenton-type, sulfate-radical, ozone-based, sonochemical, plasma-assisted and hybrid systems. Parent 2,4-D removal or analytical confirmation was reported in 202 studies, while carbon-based mineralization or organic-load evidence was reported in 116, transformation products in 95, residual toxicity in 27, real-water validation in 67 and reactor-scale or transferability information in 37. These patterns show stronger evidence for parent-compound disappearance than for treatment completeness, residual hazard and transferability. No AOP family was universally superior across removal, mineralization, toxicity reduction, matrix robustness, energy demand, durability and scale readiness. Future studies should standardize reporting of mineralization, transformation products, toxicity, energy boundaries, leaching, durability and reactor descriptors.
nfbe90dfa6f81: This study investigated the recovery and nanoliposomal formulation of anthocyanin-rich extracts from black rice using choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs). Choline chloride/1,2-propanediol (DES2) produced the highest anthocyanin content, 85.5 ± 3.4 mg l−1, after optimization, compared with 25.7 ± 2.1 mg l−1 obtained by conventional ethanol extraction. High-resolution QTOF-MS/MS enabled the tentative assignment of cyanidin 3-O-hexoside-type and peonidin 3-O-hexoside-type compounds based on accurate precursor masses and characteristic product ions; authentic-standard confirmation was not performed. The DES2 extract showed greater apparent thermal stability than the control extract, with estimated half-lives of 30.0 and 16.0 days, respectively, at 45°C. Anti-oxidant activity was observed in DPPH and ABTS assays, with IC50 values of 0.19 ± 0.06 and 0.16 ± 0.08 mg ml−1, respectively. Preliminary antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli was detected under the tested agar-diffusion conditions, whereas activity against Staphylococcus aureus was limited. Nanoliposomal encapsulation achieved an encapsulation efficiency of 73.8 ± 4.3%, a Z-average diameter of 201.3 nm and 89.83 ± 0.65% anthocyanin retention after 28 days at 4°C. The formulation produced a larger inhibition zone against E. coli than the free extract under the assay conditions. These findings support further investigation, although release kinetics, pharmaceutical efficacy and complete-process sustainability remain unestablished.
n58801560c7be: After the leakage of a buried pipeline, the overlying soil structure deforms under the high-speed impact of escaping gas, influencing both leakage and diffusion behaviours. This deformation typically appears as a soil cavity above the leakage port, especially in medium- and low-pressure conditions. In this study, the formation process of soil cavities is investigated using CFD–DEM coupled numerical simulations. The control variable method is applied to examine how different conditions affect cavity size and gas diffusion, and the sensitivity between cavity characteristics and leakage behaviour is analysed. Results show that the leaked gas forms a high-velocity zone near the leakage port, generating negative pressure in the surrounding area. Soil cavities generally form and stabilize within 0.1 s under gas impact. Soil particle size and porosity significantly influence the cavity formation time by altering the pore structure and total pore volume. The average sensitivity coefficients of the maximum cavity width to gas leakage velocity and the highest dangerous range (HDR) are 5.71 and 18.78, respectively, indicating that larger cavity widths correspond to higher leakage velocities and greater HDR. Therefore, the maximum cavity width serves as the most appropriate indicator for evaluating soil cavities caused by buried gas pipeline leakage.
n22e69b0de952: Urbanization poses a drastic threat to biodiversity, but does not affect all species equally. As such, identifying the life history traits and ecological characteristics that distinguish species that tolerate urban areas from those that do not is a central goal in urban ecology. Additionally, understanding whether shared evolutionary history influences urban tolerance could shed light on its evolutionary origins and reveal the extent to which urban landscapes filter out entire taxonomic clades, homogenizing biodiversity. Here, we assessed the relationship between urban tolerance and eight different life history and ecological traits for 431 North American bird species. We found that birds with higher urban tolerance are longer-lived, smaller-bodied, and more likely to be sedentary or mixed migrants than birds with lower urban tolerance. Birds with higher urban tolerance also have broader environmental tolerance, based on breeding range size and estimates of range-wide variation in precipitation, consistent with their greater likelihood of being habitat generalists. We additionally detected a phylogenetic signal for urban tolerance, with several clades sharing similar urban tolerance measures. Our study identifies several mechanisms that likely underlie species differences in urban tolerance and demonstrates how urban areas can filter bird species based on their life history and ecological traits.
n16111fed2f84: Many animals defend themselves with toxic chemicals and use multimodal warning displays involving odours and bright colours to advertise their toxicity. Yet, how coloration and odour interact and why they so often evolve together is not well understood. Recent work in jumping spiders has shown that defensive odours from three chemically defended bugs (Order Hemiptera: Acanthocephala femorata, Mormidea sp. and Leptoglossus phyllopus) increase a foraging aversion to red prey. Here, we ask whether these odours also increase avoidance of another visual warning: high-contrast stripes. Jumping spiders (Habronattus trimaculatus) were given choices between pattern-manipulated termites (solid white and black-and-white striped) in the presence or absence of a defensive odour from one of the aforementioned bug species. We predicted that any aversion to stripes would be stronger when odour was present. Surprisingly, we found no effect of any bug odour on the spiders’ aversions to stripes. Interestingly, these odours that so strongly and consistently trigger aversion to red do not have the same effect on stripes. This highlights the different ways that odours and coloration can interact (or not) to influence predators, providing insight into the diversity of aposematic displays in nature.
n74f0a6ed12d1: Parent–offspring communication depends on offspring signals that help parents assess need and allocate care. Nestling begging is often treated as a graded, information-rich and therefore honest signal of hunger, as predicted by costly signalling models. We quantified how effectively visual and acoustic begging components encode food deprivation in spotless starling (Sturnus unicolor) nestlings using field observations and a controlled laboratory experiment. We combined random-regression models with information-theoretic measures of uncertainty reduction and receiver-based machine-learning decoding. In wild broods, begging order and maximum postural intensity increased with deprivation time, yet posture and calling together reduced uncertainty about deprivation by less than 5%. Distinct postural levels overlapped widely among deprivation states and followed a stereotyped sequence—rapid escalation to maximum intensity followed by relaxation—yielding poor resolution of intermediate hunger. Adding components improved decoding only marginally beyond the first few cues. Parental allocation was correspondingly rapid, although display duration could provide additional information once the full bout was perceived. Discrete coding analyses confirmed that simple postural schemes were most consistent and that begging reliably distinguished only coarse, extreme hunger states. Overall, the results support partially informative (pooling) or attention-seeking signalling models in which parents rely on a small set of salient cues within a multi-component display.
n98b2558dccf9: Social isolation measures enforced during the COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of the social environment in shaping affective states and decision-making. However, the day-to-day experience and psychological recovery from social deprivation, especially among individuals with high trait anxiety, remains poorly understood. We conducted a 10-day longitudinal study with 116 university students returning to campus, collecting approximately 31 000 momentary assessments of affect and social interactions during a 3-day quarantine and subsequent period. Quarantine increased the need for social interaction and altered patterns of social engagement, whereas trait anxiety was robustly associated with reduced positive affect and elevated negative affect. Close interactions following quarantine were associated with higher positive affect. We also administered a virtual patch-foraging task to participants during and after quarantine. Greater variability in negative affect was associated with lower patch exit thresholds, suggesting a tendency to persist in depleted patches. These findings highlight how trait anxiety shapes emotional experience and social behaviour in daily life and reveal how fluctuations in negative affect can influence sequential decision-making under uncertainty.
n4b076bcf5895: Changes in the axial skeleton played an important role in dinosaur evolution, with some of the oldest dinosaurs showing evidence of sacralization events. The increased number of early dinosaur discoveries over the last decade provides an opportunity to better characterize this phenomenon. It has led us to revise our understanding of axial evolution in early dinosaurs. Results support that the last common ancestor of Dinosauria would probably present 9 cervical, 16 dorsal and 2 sacral vertebrae (primordials). Early saurischians maintain a consistent number of vertebrae with presacral origin, and there is no evidence of meristic changes in these dinosaurs. A more complex scenario is observed in early ornithischians (including ‘silesaurids’). An insertion between the primordials occurs early in ornithischian evolution, and it appears to be maintained in ‘traditional’ ornithischians (Saphornithischia). Unambiguous evidence supports loss and gain of presacral vertebrae in ornithischians. Inserted sacrals across all dinosaurs are associated with a loss of a corresponding dorsal vertebra, supporting that these represent trunk vertebrae moved into the sacrum rather than novel vertebral unities. Changes in the axial skeleton of early dinosaurs are dominated by homeotic processes, with meristic processes restricted to derived members.
n48ca4bc88a65: The material properties of bone in the skull are known to be heterogeneous and orthotropic, although datasets detailing these properties on a species level are limited. Therefore, computational modelling frequently uses homogeneous, isotropic material properties to analyse stresses/strains in the skull. However, it is often unknown how the choice of bone/s from which the elastic modulus is measured, or the direction in which it is measured, influences predicted stresses/strains. This study integrated imaging and measured muscle properties to create a subject-specific finite element model of a rabbit (Oryctolagus cuniculus) skull, to investigate the influence of modelling the elastic modulus of bone through varying levels of complexity. The results demonstrate the importance of modelling orthotropic material properties, if known. Strain distribution was insensitive to whether the same isotropic elastic modulus was used for all bones in the skull versus modelling bone-specific isotropic elastic modulus. Strain distribution was also similar when using an isotropic elastic modulus based on measurement in different orthotropic directions, albeit with a slight difference when measured in the medio-lateral direction. This highlights that isotropic, homogeneous modelling of the skull is appropriate when analysing strain distribution, although alternative material modelling should be considered when strain magnitude is of particular interest.
ndacf7e2b40da: Groundwater-dependent ecosystems are biodiversity hotspots that provide habitat for specialized species. The European Union (EU) Water Framework Directive (WFD) stresses the importance of identifying and protecting these ecosystems. So far, most studies focus on (semi-) arid regions, where groundwater use by ecosystems is both more prevalent and easier to detect. In this study, we adapt groundwater-dependent vegetation (GDV) mapping approaches developed for dry climates to temperate regions by replacing seasonal drought-based indicators with contrasts between dry and wet years. We implement this concept by integrating for the first time to our knowledge, ECOSTRESS evapotranspiration data with high-resolution remote sensing, regional geospatial data and botanical field observations. To test our framework, we trained and validated random forest models with eight predictor variables using 166 vegetation plots to identify GDV in Central Germany. Ground-truth GDV plots prefer cooler, wetter, nutrient-richer and more acidic to alkaline environments compared to non-GDV. The final model using a phreatophyte cover threshold of 25% representing GDV plots achieved a testing accuracy of 0.97, identifying 2067 km² of GDV. Currently, only 19% is protected under the EU WFD. The proposed mapping framework offers a solution for identifying GDV in temperate regions. The new GDV maps can contribute to managing groundwater resources and preserving biodiversity hotspots in regions facing increasing droughts, ultimately supporting the implementation of the EU WFD.
n757380213509: Climatic variation can shape primate activity budgets by altering the energetic and thermoregulatory costs of feeding, resting, locomotion and social behaviour. However, little is known about how chimpanzees that inhabit cool, wet montane forests adjust their activity in response to fine-scale meteorological conditions. We examined the effects of temperature, absolute humidity (water vapour pressure (WVP)), wind speed and rainfall on eastern chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes schweinfurthii) in Nyungwe National Park, Rwanda, one of the highest-elevation chimpanzee habitats. From March 2024 to February 2025, we collected 1933 party scans and 5661 individual scans, together with scan-level microclimatic measurements. Rainfall showed the clearest behavioural association: feeding probability declined during rainfall, whereas resting increased. Wind speed was negatively associated with both locomotion and grooming, suggesting that windier conditions may constrain movement and social behaviour. Temperature, WVP and fruit availability showed no clear association with any of the four behaviours. Feeding probability was higher and resting probability lower in the wet season than in the dry season. Harmonic beta-binomial generalized linear mixed-effects models revealed pronounced daily rhythmicity in feeding and resting. Overall, Nyungwe chimpanzees maintained broadly conserved daily activity rhythms while selectively adjusting behavioural allocation in response to immediate meteorological conditions.
na44cd5eb6c38: Development of sustainable hydrogen production methods is crucial for the future hydrogen economy. Hence, designing cheap, stable and efficient catalysts for hydrogen generation is important. Here, we present the use of the family of eight Schiff base ligand-based transition metal complexes [MnIII(Salen)Cl] 1/[CoII(Salen)], 2/[NiII(Salen)], 3/[CuII(Salen)], 4/[MnIII(CH3Salen)Cl], 5/[CoII(CH3Salen)], 6/[NiII(CH3Salen)], 7/[CuII(CH3Salen)] and 8 (Salen/N,N′-bis(salicylidene)ethylenediamine/H2L1; CH3Salen/N,N′-bis(o-hydroxyacetophenone)ethylenediamine/H2L2) as hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts. Electrochemical studies for the complexes (in CH3CN) were carried out in the absence and presence of acids. Catalytic parameters of turnover frequency/overpotential were calculated for the electrocatalytic process. All complexes were found to be efficient HER catalysts in the presence of acids and Co/Ni/Cu complexes were more stable than the Mn complexes. The stability and efficiency order of the catalysts was 2, 4 > 6 > 7 > 3 > 8 (acetic acid); 1 > 5 (trifluoroacetic acid). Density functional theory studies provided detailed insight into the metal- versus ligand-centred redox transitions and the HER mechanism for all complexes. Successive events of electrochemical reduction (E) and protonation (C) along the HER paths were investigated, and thermodynamically feasible routes were assigned. This work provides insights into the effect of a series of earth-abundant transition metal complex structures, the performance of this series of metal centres on electrocatalysis, and the effect of pKa on reactivity. Hence, it will be of value to develop novel and promising catalysts for HER in the future.
nb699c2f6b386: Aggressive and affiliative interactions shape resource allocation, social structure and reproduction in social species. In delphinids, rake marks (parallel scars from tooth raking) indicate social interactions. When examined alongside ontogeny, demographic traits and scar position, rake marks can inform social dynamics. We assessed rake marks on common dolphins (Delphinus delphis) in Aotearoa New Zealand (2006–2024; n = 102) during post-mortem examinations to explore drivers of social behaviour. Using a zero-inflated generalized linear mixed model, we assessed rake mark occurrence (probability of rake density > 0) and prevalence (rake density, rake marks dm−2) across the body (n = 101; dorsal/ventral, cranial/caudal, left/right) in relation to sex, age, total body length (TBL), sexual maturity, body condition (n = 101) and female reproductive status (n = 51), to infer confrontation, avoidance and lateralization. Females showed higher rake mark prevalence but lower occurrence than males, suggesting infrequent but prolonged interactions, possibly sexual coercion. Rake prevalence and occurrence increased with TBL, potentially related to increased social interactions and surface area in larger individuals. Age, sexual maturity, body condition, and female reproductive status were not strong predictors of rake mark occurrence or prevalence. Our findings highlight rake marks as potential indicators of social dynamics.
n2165ce6e22a8: Polyethylene (PE) is a highly recalcitrant polymer that resists microbial degradation owing to its hydrophobic and chemically inert structure. In this study, a Streptomyces sp. strain MH-1, isolated from the earthworm gut, was investigated for its interaction with PE under carbon-limited conditions. The strain was associated with approximately 15% reduction in PE weight after 30 days of incubation. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) analysis revealed alterations in polymer chemistry, including a reduction in the carbonyl peak (approx. 1715 cm‒1) and a decrease in the carbonyl index from 0.19 in the control to 0.10 in treated samples. In silico analysis using a closely related Streptomyces genome as a reference framework identified putative genes associated with hydrocarbon metabolism and suggested potential oxidative and assimilatory pathways. Candidate aldehyde dehydrogenases, including bifunctional alcohol/aldehyde dehydrogenase (adhE), together with genes associated with fatty acid metabolism and β-oxidation, may indicate potential mechanisms involved in the processing of oxidation intermediates. These findings, combined with biofilm formation and growth under confined conditions, highlight the importance of PE-associated microenvironments and provide a basis for exploring microbial adaptation and potential metabolic processes involved in PE biotransformation.
n99889e712f21: Although interspecific morphological diversity in aquatic animals often reflects swimming-related functional trade-offs, whether intraspecific morphological variation, often generated by phenotypic plasticity, also reflects similar trade-offs remains unclear. We tested this hypothesis using Rana pirica tadpoles, which exhibit a dragonfly-induced phenotype with a deeper tail and a salamander-induced phenotype with both a deeper tail and a swollen body. Fast-start swimming speed was highest in the dragonfly-induced phenotype, intermediate in the salamander-induced phenotype and lowest in the non-induced phenotype. Because swimming speed is influenced by both morphology and body-motion effort, we quantified motion–speed efficiency (Ems) as an index of morphological effects on swimming performance. Both predator-induced phenotypes exhibited higher Ems than the non-induced phenotype, despite similar tail-motion quantity among phenotypes, with the highest value in the dragonfly-induced phenotype. These results indicate that the shared deeper tail more efficiently converts body-motion effort into swimming speed, whereas in the salamander-induced phenotype, this function is partly offset by increased hydrodynamic drag caused by its swollen body, a morphology that protects against swallowing by gape-limited salamander larvae. These results demonstrate that predator-induced morphologies involve functional trade-offs between swimming escape and physical protection and suggest that such trade-offs contribute to morphological diversification through phenotypic plasticity.
n2e6cf7fc8bb9: Proteomic analysis is a fundamental tool for obtaining new information about biological functions that occur at the molecular level in the body, allowing the understanding of physiological and pathological processes, as well as contributing to the diagnosis and prevention of diseases. However, a critical step for the success of these analyses is the protein extraction from the tissue of interest, with well-described and reproducible protocols still scarce in the current literature, especially for bone tissues. Therefore, the main objective of this study was to present a reliable and standardized methodology for protein extraction from hard tissue samples. The methodology employed was based on an extraction protocol using demineralized bone tissue, with more detailed experimental parameters such as incubation times, temperatures and sample storage conditions. As a result, 1429 proteins previously described for the species Rattus norvegicus were identified, along with 138 uncharacterized proteins and the detection of signalling pathways strongly associated with bone metabolism. The proposed protocol has the potential for adaptation to different experimental contexts, being adjustable for various species and types of bone, considering variations in density, degree of mineralization and structural characteristics of the analysed tissue.
n1c0fdb235e43: We aimed to generate institution-level data of indicators that may reflect, as proxies, the impact and the research integrity of the authors affiliated with them and that also adjust for institution size and scientific subfields where these authors work. We used the Scopus database to generate institution-level data on top-cited authors (according to a composite citation indicator) and three indicators that may reflect problems with research integrity: the total number of authorships in papers retracted for reasons other than publisher/journal errors, and subfield-adjusted proportions of top-cited authors who have high (>95% percentile) self-citation rates or high (>95% percentile) rates of publications in Scopus-discontinued titles. There was modest overlap among top institutions based on volume and based on number of top-cited authors. However, there was minimal overlap when institutions with the highest proportions of top-cited authors were considered; these included mostly research institutes and tech organizations and only a minority of universities. Institutions with the highest self-citation, discontinuation and retraction penalties clustered in specific countries such as Saudi Arabia, People's Republic of China, Malaysia, Iran, India and Indonesia. The publicly available datasets that we provide allow the exploration of institution-level research assessments that balance high impact against proxies of diverse aspects of research integrity.
n2dbea0a14a3e: How closely related, ecologically similar species co-occur and navigate competition remains a central question in community ecology. Microhabitat partitioning in patchy environments can support the co-existence of sympatric species on small spatial scales. We quantified niche spaces and directional niche overlaps of three cold-adapted, high-altitude pikas (Ochotona spp.) from the Trans-Himalayas to understand their responses to interspecific competition across elevational and spatial scales. Vegetation- and landscape-level features were documented across elevational bands. The social, burrowing O. nubrica preferred tall stands and high shrub cover on pastures (2800–4500 m). Conversely, the social, burrowing O. ladacensis emerged as a high-elevation specialist (4200–6000 m), occupying stunted alpine scrub and steppes. The asocial, rock-dwelling O. macrotis preferred microhabitats with high rock cover across elevations (2800–6000 m), associating with significantly greener microhabitats at lower elevations in summer. Visualizing directional niche overlaps revealed scale-dependent patterns of niche segregation; species functioning as generalists at large spatial scales behaved as specialists at smaller scales. As climate change and shifting land-use patterns threaten cold-adapted Himalayan specialists, this nuanced understanding of microhabitat associations in sympatric zones is vital for informing conservation planning.
na292b00abb08: Obsidian—natural volcanic glass—was exploited for millennia and played a central role in the technological and socio-economic development of pre-Hispanic societies across Mesoamerica. The selection of obsidian from specific deposits has been linked to differences in visual appearance and patterns of use; however, the material properties underlying these preferences remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate obsidians from the Sierra de Las Navajas deposit—the most exploited obsidian deposit in Mesoamerica. We combine ball-on-three-ball measurements to quantify fracture strength with nanoindentation to quantify hardness, complemented by X-ray tomography and scanning electron microscopy. Mechanical behaviour varies among obsidian families and sampling locations and is primarily controlled by textural characteristics, notably the size and morphology of inclusions. These textures reflect distinct volcanic processes that govern material performance. Our results establish the first quantitative framework linking volcanic textures and mechanical performance in obsidians from Sierra de Las Navajas, providing a physical basis for evaluating how geological processes may have influenced obsidian utilization in pre-Hispanic Mesoamerica.
n83cd880dfd35: Most fish species are ectothermic and rely on behavioral strategies to control their body temperature in heterothermal environments. Both thermotaxis and thermokinesis have been suggested as important underlying mechanisms. However, to what extent these behaviors allow fish to respond to rapid (timescales of minutes) and strong thermal disturbances, like those caused by anthropogenic water releases into natural freshwater systems, is poorly understood. Here, we quantify this response for a salmonid species with a novel laboratory approach coupled with image-based tracking. We exposed brown trout parr (Salmo trutta), acclimated to 12 °C, to rapidly forming cold- and warm-water interfaces with temperatures ranging from 4 to 20 °C. We found that fish actively avoided colder water (≤8 °C) through a rapid response that combined thermotaxis and thermokinesis. In contrast, fish did not avoid warmer water and frequently crossed interfaces having temperature contrasts of up to 8 °C. This study shows that brown trout parr swiftly deploy multiple behavioral strategies to minimize exposure to cold water and take advantage of warm water, illustrating their capability to cope with rapidly occurring thermal alterations.
n9f3420dadd55: Large language models are very good at providing concise answers. But if we only see the answer without knowing the original question or the context behind it, that answer may not be very useful. The important issue is not simply how much information an AI summary removes but whether we can still recover the missing context. Thus, AI literature tools should also report how much information was removed and how recoverable their omissions are.
n33e0684429ce: A negative contains all the information for the final photographic print. But held up against the light, the negative often appears glaring and garish—certainly unfamiliar and sometimes difficult to recognize. Immediately after exposure in the quiet acrid environment of the darkroom, the positive enlargement is initially invisible and then starts to appear so faintly that it is scarcely detectable; only with patience as it reacts to the harsh chemical baths into which it was plunged does it emerge into a sharp, detailed, and nuanced image. In the shadows cast by the negative, as the resultant positive emerges from the nearly unrecognizable past, it is surprising and gratifying to discover a memory of the initial moment of exposure. This metaphor serves as an apt though abstract description of the experiences described in this essay.
n734296b614f3: The clonal raider ant, Ooceraea biroi , is a blind, subterranean insect that combines several rare life history traits which make it uniquely suited for use as a laboratory model. The species has lost the queen caste; instead, colonies are composed entirely of clonally reproducing workers. Workers lay eggs in synchrony, giving rise to discrete and age-matched cohorts of new workers. Despite this simple biology, the clonal raider ant displays sophisticated social and collective behaviors, including scout-initiated group raids of live arthropod prey as well as regular colony emigrations. The species also relies heavily on pheromones and other olfactory signals to mediate general ant behaviors such as trail following, alarm responses, worker policing, and nonnestmate discrimination. Here, I discuss how the clonal raider ant provides unprecedented access to study these and other social insect behaviors with modern molecular tools.
n341d4a0f3cf5: The incorporation of scientific methods into redistricting litigation has generated considerable optimism. However, for politically charged disputes such as redistricting, embedding scientific rigor within the judicial process faces substantial hurdles. The adversarial process, by design, is inclined to reward rhetorical force over epistemic integrity. While science may provide important insight, to gain such insight we must guard against its distortion and strategic misuse. Ultimately, we must also realize that the task of defining fairness in political representation is a deeply philosophical and normative exercise that belongs to the polity and its democratic institutions, where science can serve in a clarifying but not determinative role.
n552e1860574d: To understand how corporate activity is changing our economies and societies, we need to distinguish how they organize through bodies of law. In general parlance, the words firm, corporation, and company are used interchangeably. This is a matter of convenience but masks how firms, as organizing units, articulate their activities through corporations as legal entities that offer them affordances. This article reviews the literature in sociolegal studies, sociology, political economy, institutional economics, and accounting studies that considers what is at stake in the firm/corporation distinction. A new way to combine their insights is offered, locating how firms use bodies of law to replicate corporate strategies and structural asymmetries in the world economy.
n75e1973f6b24: Empirical legal researchers often seek to make causal inferences about a class of phenomena that we call selectiony treatments: treatments that are defined by some reasons, rules, or mechanisms that bring them about. Reviewing the literature, we suggest that these types of treatments suffuse the law, because the law is all about limiting the kinds of reasons that can serve as the grounds for a particular legal status. Selectiony treatments pose a distinctive conceptual problem for causal inference: They make it difficult to define counterfactual contrasts that correspond to real-world interventions of interest. We show how this problem surfaces in the study of canonical legal phenomena like bail, incarceration, and police stops, and we clarify how it differs from familiar concerns like confounding and selection bias. We provide a clear way for researchers to think through these issues and diagnose limitations to their causal inferences by emphasizing two prerequisites for coherent causal claims: ( a ) a clear definition of the variables inside a causal model and ( b ) a clear understanding of the causal estimand that is its target.
nd3a7d355e73f: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is caused by one of the most common single gene defects in humans and has severe clinical consequences that affect millions of individuals worldwide. It is well established that sufficient levels of fetal hemoglobin (HbF) postnatally can abrogate the pathophysiologic cause of red cell sickling and hence the morbid manifestations of SCD. Major advances in understanding the basis for developmental globin gene regulation and postnatal HbF silencing in recent years have uncovered the detailed molecular mechanisms involved. These discoveries have led to curative gene therapy and identified potential targets for small-molecule therapeutics that could induce similarly high levels of HbF. Successful development of drugs based on knowledge about the molecular mechanisms of HbF silencing would meet a pressing need for treatments that induce sufficient HbF to prevent the morbidity of SCD and that may be accessible in the near future for the majority of affected individuals worldwide.
n975bda822455: Ninety-eight percent of the human transcriptome lacks protein-coding potential. A small fraction of this landscape comprises housekeeping noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs) with well-defined functions, whereas the heterogeneous group of regulatory ncRNAs, generated from ∼100,000 loci, acts through diverse mechanisms to control gene expression, chromatin states, RNA processing, and signaling networks. Their recent evolutionary expansion reflects the increasing regulatory complexity of cell and tissue specification programs in higher organisms. In cancer, such programs are co-opted, with fine-tuned regulatory control contributing to the rewiring of molecular networks during transformation, metastasis, and adaptation to therapy. Here, we review the molecular functions of ncRNAs and their involvement in cancer, with emphasis on regulatory classes including microRNAs, long noncoding RNAs, and circular RNAs. We also describe emerging technical innovations that advance their investigation, including genetic tools enabling systematic, context-resolved mapping of ncRNA functions. We conclude by discussing the translational potential of ncRNAs as biomarkers and therapeutic targets.
ne110791198cb: Environmental chemicals and toxicants can promote phenotypic variation or disease not only in the individual exposed but also in individuals for multiple subsequent generations. This phenomenon is termed epigenetic transgenerational inheritance and generational toxicology. Most environmental factors and toxicants do not promote genetic mutations that alter the DNA sequence, but they can alter epigenetics and the epigenome. Epigenetic changes in the germline allow for epigenetic transgenerational inheritance and generational toxicology as a result of the previous generations’ exposures. The toxicology and pharmacology of environmental chemicals and epigenetic transgenerational inheritance are discussed in the context of generational toxicology.
nef412af17fca: Neurons represent changes in external and internal environments by altering their activity patterns. While coherent brain-wide patterns of neural activity have been observed in neuronal populations, very little is known about their dimensionality, geometry, and how they are correlated with sensory inputs. Here, we recorded the activity of most head neurons in Caenorhabditis elegans experiencing changes in bacterial or control buffer stimuli around their nose. We first classified active neurons into six functional clusters: two sensory neuron clusters (ON and OFF responding to addition and removal of stimuli, respectively) and four motor/command neuron clusters (AVA, RME, SMDD, and SMDV). Next, we estimated stimulus selectivity for each cluster and found that while sensory neurons exhibit their maximal responses within 15 s, changes in bacterial stimuli drive maximal responses in command and motor neuron clusters after tens of seconds. Furthermore, we show that bacterial stimuli induce neural dynamics that are best described by a hyperbolic, not Euclidean, space indicating hierarchical organization in C. elegans neural population dynamics. This space was 8-dimensional, with dimensions that aligned in one sensory direction (ON and OFF neurons), two motor directions (forward-backward and dorsal-ventral), and the rest of dimensions corresponding with unclassified neurons. Collectively, we show that C. elegans neural activity can be effectively represented in low-dimensional hyperbolic space and describe how sensory information is processed by the neural network.
n7d6adc2ffcb6: Human Leukocyte Antigen (HLA)-G is selectively expressed by fetal trophoblast cells that encounter maternal natural killer (NK) cells early in pregnancy. In response to HLA-G, the endosomal NK cell receptor KIR2DL4 induces a transcriptional program to support placental development. Structural features of KIR2DL4 that control HLA-G binding and endocytosis are unclear. Random mutagenesis revealed that three cysteines in the first immunoglobulin domain of KIR2DL4 regulate endocytosis and uptake of HLA-G. The atypical Cys10–Cys28 disulfide bond in the KIR2DL4 structure is an allosteric disulfide with potential to switch to a conventional Cys28–Cys74 bond. KIR2DL4 in human cells exists in both disulfide-bonded states, as shown by mass spectrometry analysis. The Cys10–Cys28 bond in a Cys74Ser KIR2DL4 mutant was reduced by protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) in vitro. Inhibition of PDI prevented HLA-G uptake by KIR2DL4 in NK cells. Mutants in the Cys10–Cys28 configuration endocytosed spontaneously but did not bind HLA-G. Conversely, KIR2DL4 with a Cys28–Cys74 bond was detectable at the plasma membrane and internalized soluble HLA-G. A purified Cys10Leu KIR2DL4 mutant bound HLA-G with micromolar affinity in a peptide-dependent manner. Thus, allosteric disulfide-mediated conversion from an inactive to an HLA-G binding form regulates KIR2DL4 trafficking and a functional response that promotes fetal development.
n8eab5f59da73: Human African trypanosomiasis (HAT) is a neglected tropical disease transmitted by infected tsetse flies (Glossina spp.) in sub-Saharan Africa. Infected tsetse flies can transmit trypanosomes, including Trypanosoma brucei subspecies that cause HAT in humans, as well as other trypanosome species that cause animal African trypanosomiasis in domestic animals and infect wildlife. Tsetse flies feed on a broad spectrum of hosts, including humans, elephants, buffaloes, rhinos, hippos, turtles, and monitor lizards. To understand how the insects can penetrate such diverse skin types, we detailed the anatomical structures involved in tsetse blood feeding, their mechanical properties, and the forces exerted by the fly during probing. We found that the tsetse fly’s feeding apparatus does not rely on exceptionally unique structures or extraordinary forces. Instead, the tsetse fly has evolved subtle yet highly efficient adaptations, which include a labellum equipped with arrays of small teeth. When combined with a robust retraction movement of the proboscis, these structures create lesions on various types of skin, thus facilitating blood pool feeding on a broad host spectrum.
n064370a640bf: Investigating the dynamics of neural networks, which are governed by connectivity between neurons, is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience. Because passive (spontaneous) activity provides only limited information for estimating connectivity, perturbation-based approaches are widely applied in neuroscience as they can evoke underlying hidden dynamics. However, the characteristics of such perturbations have typically been designed based on empirical or biological intuition. To enable more accurate estimation of connectivity, we propose a data-driven and theoretically grounded framework for optimally designing perturbation inputs, based on formulating the neural model as a control system. The core theoretical insight underlying our approach is that neural signals observed in the passive state lack sufficient latent information, which leads to failures in the system identification. Perturbations reveal these hidden dynamics and lead to improved estimation. Guided by these insights, we derive a theoretical basis for optimizing perturbation inputs that minimize estimation errors in neural system identification. Building upon this, we further explore the relationship of this theory with stimulation patterns commonly used in neuroscience, such as frequency, impulse, and step inputs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework for neuroscience through simulations grounded in experimental paradigms, such as neural state classification and optimal control of neural states. Our theoretical analysis, together with multiple simulations, consistently shows that perturbations designed according to our framework achieve substantially more accurate system identification compared to the conventional, intuition-based inputs. This study provides a theoretical foundation for designing perturbation inputs to achieve accurate estimation of neural dynamics. This, in turn, enables reliable discrimination of neural states such as levels of consciousness and pathological conditions, and facilitates precise control of their transitions toward recovery from abnormal states.
n8c5e9d26a1ec: Neural circuit assembly relies on the precise regulation of cell-surface receptors that mediate signaling and adhesion. Endocytosis controls receptor activity and availability by internalizing and routing proteins through early endosomes to one of two main pathways: recycling back to the cell-surface or delivery to lysosomes for degradation. Rab GTPases direct receptors into these distinct pathways, but their specific contributions to circuit formation remain opaque. Using clonal analyses with null alleles, we dissected the roles of Rab-mediated trafficking to early, late, and recycling endosomes across multiple stages of circuit assembly in vivo. Our approach revealed that Rab5 and Rab11 regulate extensive and largely distinct developmental events, highlighting the pivotal roles of early endosome sorting and recycling pathways in circuit assembly. As neurons mature, both the spatial distribution and abundance of specific endocytic compartments change to reflect evolving trafficking demands. Our findings underscore how distinct post-endocytic trafficking fates are necessary to build neural circuits.
n26830a9e154a: Glycogen phosphorylase (GP) catalyzes the rate-limiting step of glycogenolysis and supplies precursors for chitin biosynthesis in insects. Acyl urea compounds structurally related to benzoylphenylurea (BPU) insecticides are potent inhibitors of mammalian GP, raising the question of whether insect GP could serve as an independent insecticidal target. Here, we show that a mammalian GP inhibitor (GPI) potently inhibits recombinant Plutella xylostella GP (PxGP; IC50=2.96 nM), while the BPU insecticide diflubenzuron does not. Molecular docking and MM/GBSA analysis predict that this selectivity reflects differential side-chain engagement. Despite potent in vitro inhibition, GPI exhibits no insecticidal activity, and RNAi-mediated knockdown of PxGP does not impair development or survival. We provide evidence that insects compensate through upregulation of gluconeogenic enzymes (PEPCK, G-6-Pase) and protein catabolism, with enzyme activity measurements confirming ~29% reduction in GP-a activity following RNAi. Fitness assessment reveals transient larval weight loss with complete recovery of pupal weight, adult morphology, and fecundity. These findings demonstrate that GP is functionally non-essential under the tested conditions, likely through gluconeogenic compensation and alternative carbon sources, and highlight the importance of metabolic network redundancy in target-based insecticide design.
n5a5175c0cfca: The JAK-STAT pathway (JSP) is a well-known oncogenic cascade; however, recent clinical trials have detected JSP upregulation in breast cancer following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. This paradoxical observation warrants further investigation into JSP’s intercellular heterogeneity, tumor dynamics, molecular mechanisms, and clinical implications for immunotherapy. JSP expression showed dynamic shifts during breast cancer progression, with higher levels in T cells and paracancerous epithelial cells. In human breast cancer tumor cells, elevated JSP is highly correlated with malignant phenotypes. JSP-high tumor cells overexpressed oncogenic pathways, while exhibiting increased immunosuppressive signaling via the MIF-CD74 signaling axis. In T cells, higher JSP levels were associated with enhanced cytotoxic activity, improved differentiation, and reduced exhaustion, reflecting robust anti-tumor immunity. Analysis of immunotherapy datasets revealed that higher JSP levels were associated with improved responses toward PD-1 inhibitors, particularly in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients, with JSP serving as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy sensitivity. As a key JSP component, STAT4 exerts dual roles in breast cancer: it drives tumorigenesis in malignant cells, sustains breast epithelial cell proliferation, and bolsters T-cell anti-tumor functionality, while also acting as a highly accurate biomarker for predicting immunotherapy response. This indicates that JSP targeting demands a nuanced approach: broad inhibition may impair anti-tumor immunity, and optimized therapeutic strategies paired with precise biomarkers are critical to maximize JSP’s utility in breast cancer immunotherapy. Our findings highlight JSP’s functional heterogeneity in epithelial, tumor, and T cells, with high JSP activity correlating with enhanced immunotherapy efficacy in breast cancer.
ncf33cbbde167: Growing evidence implicates the hippocampus in the pathophysiology of autism spectrum disorder, particularly in the domains of social interactions and cognition. Yet, the mechanisms driving the hippocampal-dependent cognitive atypicalities in autism remain poorly defined. Here, we characterized how dysfunction of the CA1 subfield of the dorsal hippocampus drives abnormalities in critical components of declarative memory. Using trace fear conditioning in the Cntnap2 knockout mouse model of autism, we found that capabilities to retain the association of temporally distant stimuli (i.e. temporal binding) were reduced relative to wildtype mice. Fiber photometry and optogenetic experiments demonstrated that reduced CA1 activity during temporal gaps underlies this impairment, linking CA1 dysfunction to a deficit in long-term memory retention in autism. Using a relational/declarative memory task, we also revealed a deficit in flexible spatial memory, and a preferential use of egocentric learning strategy. This inflexible learning strategy resulted from an imbalance between memory system activity, promoting frontostriatal-dependent procedural learning instead of dorsal CA1/hippocampus-dependent relational/declarative memory. Overall, this study establishes dorsal CA1 dysfunction as a circuit-level mechanism underlying cognitive inflexibility in autism, providing a neurobiological framework for hippocampal-dependent memory deficits in the condition.
nca3eac692978: Many jurisdictions have sought to mitigate hurdles faced by people with criminal records by allowing those records to be expunged (or sealed). Expungement eliminates most legal restrictions triggered by records, and policymakers hope it could also improve access to employment and housing markets and reduce social stigma. Yet there remain significant questions about how well this intervention works. This article canvasses the nascent empirical literature on expungement, focusing on three areas. First, uptake studies consistently find that when eligible individuals must file legal petitions for expungement, only a small fraction do so. Second, studies of those who do receive petition-based expungement have mostly found positive effects on employment and other outcomes. However, the uptake problem introduces sample selection concerns that complicate causal inference, and one recent randomized control trial found a disappointing absence of effects. Third, research on automated expungement (carried out by the state without individuals petitioning) is especially limited, but there is some reason for skepticism about its effects, at least on employment.
nc0b7b171a689: This review centers on the development of labeling theory in criminology. Our core argument is that modifications to labeling theory in the past several decades have veered research away from the theory's core propositions. We extend this argument by presenting a three-part conceptual model of secondary deviance, defined as persistence in deviant behavior as a result of punishment. First, a subtheory of punishment and social exclusion explains institutional and interpersonal exclusion after punishment as the result of selection, separation, and stigma. Stigma manifests as rejection, withdrawal, and homophily. Second, deviant identity is reintroduced as the central motivating mechanism of secondary deviance. Its development involves the links between actual and reflected appraisals and the internalization of reflected appraisals into self-appraisals. Third, peer and community contexts are sources of variation in the effects of punishment on social exclusion and deviant identity. Researchers should give special attention to how these processes unfold within individuals and across life stages. Our model serves as a framework for advancing understanding of the mechanisms that drive criminogenic consequences of punishment.
nfe6d350af04f: Police violence remains pervasive across democratic societies in the Americas. This review brings the US literature on policing into dialogue with comparative research on Latin America to identify common forces that sustain what we call punitive policing—systems of law enforcement that systematically violate human rights, rely on excessive surveillance and coercion, and disproportionately target marginalized populations. Synthesizing scholarship from both regions, the review highlights three factors that help explain the persistence of punitive policing: colonial legacies, the militarization of public security, and deeply entrenched racial and socioeconomic inequalities that shape how police are deployed and whom they target with violence. Our review shows that punitive policing is a governance problem that undermines legitimacy, public safety, citizenship, and democratic stability. Yet the evidence also suggests that meaningful reform is possible when bottom-up, coordinated mobilization converges with top-down institutional intervention to constrain punitive policing.
n2712d9bba975: Scholars of mass incarceration have tended to understand the prison as a labor market institution mostly in the negative sense: as a warehouse for those otherwise likely to be unemployed and as a site of status degradation that further reduces people's ability to find employment after release. In this article, we review recent work that has focused attention on the prison as a labor market institution in a more productive sense: as an organization that shapes the work activity of the many workers incarcerated within it, facilitates formerly incarcerated people's subordination in the labor market upon release, and may play a more active role than previously imagined in shaping the distribution of jobs available in the US labor market as a whole. We also introduce new evidence that the tightness of the labor market structures how a criminal record shapes people's labor market experiences after incarceration.
n19158c5f9c67: Fish schools are among the most spectacular examples of collective behavior in nature. Individual fish coordinate their motion with neighbors primarily through vision and flow sensing. Each fish generates flow disturbances that can influence the motion and energetics of nearby swimmers. Yet fundamental questions remain unresolved: To what extent can schooling be explained by passive hydrodynamic interactions, and where are individual-level sensing and control required to maintain group cohesion? This review examines collective swimming through the lens of fluid mechanics. By synthesizing experimental, theoretical, and computational studies spanning pairs of fish to large schools, I discuss how hydrodynamic interactions affect coordination, stability, and energetic cost. Flow interactions can yield robust pairwise coordination and locomotor benefits, but they can also drive collective instabilities and unequal benefit distributions in larger groups. These findings point to a fundamental interplay between hydrodynamics and sensory–motor feedback in the formation and maintenance of fish schools. More broadly, they suggest that hydrodynamics shapes collective swimming not only through energetic costs and benefits but also through the physical constraints it imposes on coordination, stability, and information flow within groups.
nd37b0c5a9cba: Cell identity is established by tightly regulated transcriptional programs. Disruption of the regulatory mechanisms governing these programs leads to aberrant behavior and, frequently, cancer. Enhancer hijacking, the process whereby a gene comes under the control of an ectopic enhancer, is a major cause of transcriptional dysregulation. Although recognized since the 1980s, its detection has been traditionally hindered by the low resolution of karyotyping and incomplete knowledge of enhancer biology. This has changed with the development of high-throughput sequencing, leading to a surge in newly identified enhancer hijacking events over the past two decades. Furthermore, functional dissection of enhancers using techniques such as CRISPR/Cas9 has shed light on their mechanistic underpinnings, with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) emerging as a paradigm for this phenomenon. In this review, we outline the historical development of enhancer hijacking, highlight representative examples in hematological malignancies, and discuss the insights derived from this research, particularly in AML.
ne665ba23399c: Circadian rhythms organize mammalian physiology across the 24-h day through molecular clocks coordinated by the central clock in the suprachiasmatic nucleus and distributed to peripheral oscillators. These clocks regulate processes central to pharmacology, including drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, elimination, and target responsiveness. Consequently, drug efficacy and toxicity can vary substantially depending on the time of administration.
